study_identification_part.si_4_title: Normative modeling analysis reveals corpus callosum volume changes in early and mid-to-late first episode major depression

dc_1_datasets_using_in_this_study.detail: The structural brain imaging data were acquired from the REST-meta-MDD Consortium, which is a collaborative effort involving twenty-five research groups from 17 hospitals in China. From this consortium, 369 first-episode MDD patients and 490 healthy controls were selected from 7 study sites after quality control and exclusion criteria.
dc_1_datasets_using_in_this_study.supporting_text: "The structural brain imaging data were acquired from the REST-meta-MDD Consortium (Chen et al., 2022; Yan et al., 2019), which is a collaborative effort involving twenty-five research groups from 17 hospitals in China."

answer.REST-meta-MDD: normative model training (healthy controls) and clinical application (first-episode MDD patients)

dc_2_purpose_of_each_dataset.detail: 490 healthy controls from the REST-meta-MDD consortium were used as the reference dataset to train the normative model via hierarchical Bayesian regression. 369 first-episode MDD patients from the same consortium were then evaluated against the normative model to obtain individual z-scores for corpus callosum (sub)volumes.
dc_2_purpose_of_each_dataset.supporting_text: "hierarchical Bayesian regression was employed to train the normative models on healthy participants (Rutherford et al., 2022)." ... "This model was further used to estimate z-scores that indicate to what extent an individual's CC volume differs from the norms calculated by the reference dataset (healthy controls)."

dc_3_number_of_healthy_control_of_each_n.detail: Only one normative model was constructed. 490 healthy controls were used as the reference dataset. The paper does not explicitly report a train/test split within the healthy control sample; the 490 HC appear to be used as the full reference cohort for the hierarchical Bayesian regression normative model.
